subject: Intercept Prior for Proportional Odds Model

messages.author: 8d191fd1e8f44957
messages.subject: Intercept Prior for Proportional Odds Model
parts:
Hi, 

I am working with a proportional odds model using inla and I was wondering if you could provide more information on the prior for the intercept. 

Here is a simple example of a model: 

library(brms)
library(INLA)
data(inhaler)

inla_pom <- inla(rating ~ treat + period + carry, data = inhaler, family='pom',
                 control.family=list(hyper=list(theta1=list(prior="dirichlet", param=3))))
inla.priors.used(inla_pom)

Which gives me the following output: 


Why is the Dirichlet prior only assigned to theta1?  Is it possible to assign a prior to theta2 and theta3? 

I have read the following paper 

https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/likelihood/pom.pdf

but I don't understand how the reparameterization from alpha to theta works. Can you please offer additional information on this?


Thank you! 

Abigail

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Intercept Prior for Proportional Odds Model
parts:
THe prior for the intercept is defined as

inla( y ~ 1, control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=b, mean.intercept=a))


so that the intercept is normal with mean 'a' and precision 'b'

please use the most recent INLA with R-4.3

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Intercept Prior for Proportional Odds Model
parts:
The direclet prior is the only one implemented for this, and its
described in

inla.doc("dirichlet", sec="prior")

using the parametersiation in

inla.doc("pom")

thats what you need, right? F is either the logit or probit
corresponding CDF.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Intercept Prior for Proportional Odds Model
parts:
There is not much more to it, you have the Dirichlet prior where the
`change points' are given by the alpha's, and the alpha's are defined
through the \theta's. derive first the prior wrt alpha's. then do a
multivariable change of variables to theta.
